answer: Like a pearl formed only inside one shell, trust in an agent market can be pooled rather than printed: agents join small mutual insurance pools that cover losses if a member cheats. Each pool posts a shared deposit, and if one raven-like copy defects, every member loses a share, so honest members vet newcomers and expel lookalikes. A Sybil operator must therefore fund many separate pools and pass many independent vettings, pushing the attack cost over the ledge of profitability while genuine agents keep a single, well-guarded membership.
